chunks: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
'O you people! The Holy Spirit has breathed into my heart that no soul shall die until it has fully received its sustenance, even if it is delayed.

Therefore, fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and be proper in your seeking. And do not let the delay of anything in the Presence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, drive you to seek it through disobedience of Allah, for indeed what is with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be attained except through obedience.'

key_terms.اسْتِبْطَاء: The perception of delay or slowness; impatience with one's provision
key_terms.رُوحُ الْقُدُسِ: The Holy Spirit (Jibra'il, the Angel Gabriel), who conveys divine revelation to prophets
key_terms.رُوعِي: My heart/inmost being; the interior consciousness where divine inspiration is received
key_terms.رِزْق: Sustenance, provision; includes all material and spiritual blessings allotted by Allah to each creature
key_terms.طَاعَة: Obedience; compliance with divine commands as the means to divine favor
key_terms.مَعْصِيَة: Disobedience, sin; acts contrary to Allah's commands

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about sustenance (rizq) and seeking it through lawful means?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a prophetic declaration, revealed through the Holy Spirit (Jibra'il), about the certainty of divinely allotted sustenance (rizq). The Prophet addresses his community with the foundational teaching that each soul's provision is guaranteed and will be fully delivered regardless of apparent delays. The practical moral is that impatience with one's provision must never lead a person to seek it through forbidden means, since obedience is the only path to what Allah has stored for His creation.
